target_customer: Autonomous vehicle and AI teams, later frontier model labs, enterprises and governments that need labeled training data and evaluation
problem: Machine learning teams needed large volumes of accurately labeled data and had to manage crowd workers themselves.
business_model: usage-based API and managed data services priced per task
product_category: AI training data and evaluation infrastructure

founders.name: Alexandr Wang
founders.background_notes: Left in 2025 to lead Meta superintelligence efforts per coverage. A second co-founder is reported elsewhere but the YC page lists only Wang; not verified here.

competitors.name: Amazon Mechanical Turk
competitors.what: General crowd work marketplace used for labeling

technical_complexity.rationale: An API that routed tasks to human labelers with quality control; the hard part was operations and quality, not research.

defensibility.rationale: Labeling was copyable; advantage came from speed, quality tooling and customer relationships, later data scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors such as Appen, Surge and Turing grew; Meta took a 49 percent stake in 2025 rather than the industry buying it outright.

market_need_then: Self-driving programs and deep learning teams in 2016 and 2017 had rising demand for ground truth data and few reliable labeling vendors.

branding.name_origin: Founder built an API that returned labeled data and called it Scale; origin per a Substack analysis, not authoritative.
branding.domain_note: Launched on scale.ai, later invested in the premium scale.com domain; date and price not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Confident and authoritative, short declarative statements

rebrands.why: Help users understand the full product suite per Scale blog

brand_strength.rationale: Widely known in AI circles as the data engine for frontier labs, but sources show little about brand assets driving growth.

pivots.to: Broader AI data engine across industries then generative AI and government

outcome_analysis: Scale used the AI data labeling boom to grow from a 2016 YC API into a company valued at 13.8 billion dollars in 2024 and tied to the largest labs as a supplier. In June 2025 Meta invested 14.3 billion dollars for 49 percent, the CEO left for Meta, Google and OpenAI reportedly wound down work, and Scale cut about 14 percent of staff in July 2025. It remains independent but faces competitors like Turing, Surge, Invisible and Labelbox.
notes: Seed amount of 120,000 dollars is a single tracker entry and likely the YC deal; Wikipedia gives a conflicting seed account. Series D (2020) and exact Series C and E investors were not found. Series A is dated July 2017 by the company blog and May 2017 by trackers. Meta round valuation not confirmed here. Wang's prior employer and MIT dropout are from general public record not re-verified in these searches.
